WEDDING ANNOUNCEMENT 
Jennie Rebecca Ripps and Max Brockman are to be married May 14, 2011 by Judge Melvyn 
Tanenbaum of the Suffolk County State Supreme Court at the Gramercy Park Hotel in New 
York City. Jennie Ripps, 30, is the President of Sponsorship Resources at Talent Resources, a 
boutique marketing firm in New York City. Ms. Ripps is also founder of The Teaologist, a tea 
company which specializes in making custom teas and tea cocktails for restaurants and hotels. 
Ms. Ripps graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 2003. 
The bride is a daughter of Susan Shapiro Barash and Richard Ripps, of New York City. Her 
mother is an author of twelve books and is a gender professor at Marymount Manhattan 
College. Her father, who is deceased, was an attorney and independent real estate developer 
of the Buckland Hills Mall in Manchester, CT and Evergreen Walk in South Windsor, CT 
Max Brockman, also 30, is the Vice President of Brockman, Inc., a literary agency specializing 
in serious non-fiction, which represents Jared Diamond, Nassim Taleb, Richard Dawkins, and 
Steven Pinker, among others. He is also the editor of two volumes of essays by young 
scientists. He graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 2002. 
The groom is the son Katinka Matson and John Brockman of New York City. His mother is the 
President of Brockman, Inc. His father is the Chairman and CEO of Brockman, Inc., and 
founder and editor of the online salonEdge.org. 
Although they attended the same university, and had mutual friends, the couple met for the first 
time at the Frankfurt Bookfair in the lobby bar of the Frankfurter Hof Hotel. At the time, Ms. 
Ripps was working for Mary Anne Thompson Associates, a literary scouting company, and 
was responsible for tracking projects at specific literary agencies and publishing houses. 
Subsequent to their meeting, Ms. Ripps requested that she be assigned to Brockman, Inc.

In the tradition of great fly-on-the-wall documentaries, PAGE ONE; INSIDE THE NEW 
YORK TIMES deftly gains unprecedented access to The New York Times newsroom and 
the inner workings of the Media Desk. With the Internet surpassing print as our main 
news source and newspapers all over the country going bankrupt, PAGE ONE 
chronicles the transformation of the media industry at its time of greatest turmoil. 
Journalists like Brian Steller, Tim Arango. the salty but brilliant David Can and their editor 
Bruce Headlam track print journalism's metamorphosis even as their own paper 
struggles to stay vital and solvent 
At the heart of the film is the burning question on the minds of everyone who cares 
about a rigorous American press. Times lover or not: what will happen if the fast-
moving future of media leaves behind the fact-based, original reporting fhaf helps to 
define our society? 
PAGE ONE opens theatrically in New York on June 17th, 2011

www.www 
Guided conversations with extraordinary individuals 
The forum shall be improvisational intellectual jazz conversations guided by a 
series of questions — not an interview however. 
The history of the evolution of this idea is as follows: 
1962 - My first book was a simple guide to understanding 50 of the world's cities 
all to the same scale. 
1967 - A guide of complex statistical analysis of 20 American cities: The MIT 
Press 
1975/76 — The initiation of guiding principals of information architecture 
manifested in my chairing a new form of gathering using the entire downtown 
Philadelphia with 5,000 attending architects at the Architecture of Information 
gathering for the annual meeting of the American Institute of Architects. The 
presenters were from varied disciplines, i.e., Jonas Salk, Buckminster Fuller and 
William Zeckendorf Sr. 
1980 — The reinvention of the modern guidebook and beginning of publishing 
more than 2 dozen books on cities, health, wealth and sports: Access Press. 
1984: In observing and reflecting upon various convergences between certain 
innovative disciplines of the late 20th century, I focused on the melding of the 
Technology business, the Entertainment industry and Design professions from 
which I created the TED Conference. 
EFTA_R1_00268801 
EFTA01865879
--- PAGE 2 ---
1995 — I created the first TEDMED conference as a guide to the possibility of 
emerging patterns in healthcare, clearly the most important discipline of our time 
using and honing the principals of TED. 
2002 — I chaired my last TED conference and sold it to a British gaming and 
business magazine publisher while maintaining TEDMED and continuing that 
series. 
2005 — I experimented with a smaller and more improvisational conference with 
the creation of eg, which I later transferred to Michael Hawley. 
2008 — I created 19.20.21. to develop a template for the comparative study of 19 
of the world's cities that will have more than 20 million people in the 215' century. 
2009 — With Marc Hodosh I re-launched TEDMED maintaining the intimacy of 
the smaller conferences and exploring more deeply the new patterns of this 
broad field, which now represents roughly 20% of the GNP.
